questions.description: How repeatable is measured exercise-specific strength or repetition-maximum performance under standardized repeat tests?
questions.gap: Ordinary submaximal training-set and e1RM repeatability in experienced hybrid athletes remains context-dependent; no individual threshold approved.

questions.description: How can comparable historical actuals and prior decisions inform bounded personal coaching choices?
questions.gap: No direct validation of the complete candidate history workflow; contextual programming judgment and separate review required.

sources.citation: Grgic J, Lazinica B, Schoenfeld BJ, Pedisic Z. Test–Retest Reliability of the One-Repetition Maximum (1RM) Strength Assessment: a Systematic Review. Sports Med Open. 2020;6:31.
sources.design: Systematic review of test-retest reliability studies
sources.publication_check: Publisher full-text article and bibliographic record inspected; dedicated correction/retraction audit remains outstanding.
sources.rights: Open-access publisher article. Catalog use limited to metadata, links and original factual summaries; independent rights review outstanding.
sources.appraisal: 32 studies, total n=1595; 14 studies included previously trained participants. COSMIN appraisal reported moderate or excellent quality; varied tests and descriptive aggregation; ICC is not absolute agreement.

sources.citation: Mitter B, Csapo R, Bauer P, Tschan H. Reproducibility of strength performance and strength-endurance profiles: A test-retest study. PLoS ONE. 2022;17(5):e0268074.
sources.publication_check: Publisher full-text article and bibliographic record inspected; dedicated correction/retraction audit remains outstanding.
sources.rights: Creative Commons Attribution license stated on publisher page. Catalog use limited to metadata, links and original factual summaries; independent rights review outstanding.
sources.appraisal: 24 trained adults, standardized pin-supported bench press; repetition tests at relative loads derived from each visit's measured 1RM. Bayesian estimates, short horizon and small sample; no evaluation of coaching policies.

claims.assertion: Measured 1RM assessments in studies including previously resistance-trained participants generally had high reported relative repeatability with variable absolute relative error.
claims.limitations: Fourteen studies with previously trained participants; mixed exercises, protocols, training experience and retest intervals. Descriptive medians and ranges, not pooled CIs.
claims.assessment: Moderate for the reported study summaries; low directness for habitual submaximal sets, e1RM or any specific hybrid athlete threshold.

support.locator: Results: Reliability in Relation to Training Status and Familiarization; Table 3 and Fig. 2.
support.restriction: Measured one-repetition maximum repeatability only; no individual change criterion or treatment effect.

claims.assertion: Repetitions to momentary failure at the tested relative bench-press loads exhibited nonzero test-retest error.
claims.limitations: 24 adults; at least one year bench training; loads recalculated from visit-specific 1RM; standardized technique/rest; not ordinary submaximal working sets.
claims.assessment: Moderate for protocol-specific posterior estimates; low directness to a personal absolute-load working set or hybrid fatigue context.

support.locator: Abstract Results; Results Table 1 and Fig. 2; Methods Experimental approach.
support.restriction: Relative loads and failure tests; interval is not an individual minimum detectable change, adjustment increment or causal effect.

methods.question: individual-history-review-methodology
methods.description: Select task- and context-comparable historical actuals as of the decision, separate current demonstrated performance from historical records, summarize exposure and observed direction, and disclose exclusions and uncertainty before ordinary bounded planning.
methods.provenance: Original candidate programming/engineering methodology, Packet 009 sections 3–4; not a tested intervention.
methods.tradeoffs: Requires comparable observations or conservative fallback; selection and window choices need review; no universal recency weight, optimal dose or latent fitness inference.

methods.question: individual-history-review-methodology
methods.description: Retain earlier approved changes and actual response; review supporting and contradictory observations in context; use tentative patterns only for relevant, feasible, reversible proposals and update on new evidence.
methods.provenance: Original candidate programming/engineering methodology, Packet 009 sections 3–4; not a tested intervention.
methods.tradeoffs: Observed association does not establish causality. Requires attributable decision and actual execution or qualified recollection; current restrictions and athlete approval govern any change. No physiological parameter estimation.
